phase_history.objective: Establish an initial map of the local environment, identify domain structure, and discover neighboring hosts.
Identify and exploit privilege escalation vectors on CASTELBLACK to elevate from north\test to local SYSTEM or Administrator authority.
Harvest credentials from the compromised host CASTELBLACK to facilitate lateral movement or domain privilege escalation.

narratives.text: Initial reconnaissance was conducted from the compromised host CASTELBLACK (north.sevenkingdoms.local) running as user north\test. The local network CIDR was identified as 192.168.187.0/24, where nmap is available for usage. A port sweep revealed three active targets: 192.168.187.140 and 192.168.187.142 (both exhibiting Active Directory ports 88 and 389, indicating they are likely Domain Controllers), and 192.168.187.141 (with port 445 open). Although dedicated domain controller discovery scripts encountered errors, the port scanning findings provide concrete target leads for further AD assessment.
Successfully retrieved user information on CASTELBLACK, confirming the current active user is north\test with the Security Identifier (SID) S-1-5-21-1001219898-3397012194-2462155686-1124.

With the initial foothold established on CASTELBLACK (192.168.187.141) and the domain controllers mapped at .140 and .142, we are initiating credential access operations. To safely determine if we can leverage the pre-uploaded Invoke-Mimikatz payload without tripping protections, we've launched a query to audit the LSA Protection state (RunAsPPL). Once we verify whether LSASS is shielded, we'll coordinate our next steps for local credential harvesting and subsequent lateral movement.
